newsitem.title: UK: LME copper above $2,000 by close, off highs.
newsitem.headline: LME copper above $2,000 by close, off highs.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices remained buoyant above $2,000 during late Friday afternoon trading, though as expected late bouts of profit-taking knocked a uptrending market from its highs.
Benchmark three months delivery copper last traded at $2,007, down $10 from Thursday and Friday's high of $2,028.
Overall the market remains in consolidation, though a further upside probe towards resistance at $2,040 is expected near term. Support is expected at $2,000, followed by a more robust area at $1,985.
Traders noted news that workers at Chile's Candelaria mine are on strike, although production has not been affected. Annual output is estimated at 150,000 tonnes a year.
Traders said an LME stocks fall of 7,775 tonnes was expected. Nearby spreads flared during the morning.
The cash to three months backwardation was bid at $74, versus earlier levels of $58/$63 and Thursday's $60 close.
Aluminium slipped under disappointed liquidation after failing to build on earlier gains up to $1,468. Freer lending of the spreads helped to dent upside sentiment.
Nickel moved higher on the back of trade and merchant demand. It was last at $7,260, up $30.
Zinc dipped in thin trading and ended $4 lower at $1,064, while lead pressured by light long liquidation settled at $735, versus $749.
Alloy was last quoted at $1,300/05, unchanged.
